# Stdlib boundary: first studies for #369 and #167

These are six actual informed authoring/observation packets retained before
production implementation of the primitive/derived-library migration. This is
not a blind benchmark. Original desired programs, current translations,
predictions, source mistakes, command-only failures, requests, real raw streams,
artifacts and binary/source identity windows remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

The [retention manifest](packets.json) lists every original member, its byte
count, SHA-256 and observed mode, together with the original temporary path.
Each archive includes the packet's own original freeze files; counts below
include those freeze files. The preserved historical plans' `executed=false`
and `UNPERFORMED` labels record authoring time, not the later observation state.

## Original findings and separate repair

The first packet contains 32 cases with desired and current programs. Its
165-member authoring freeze predates execution. The 128 first source checks
accepted 40 and refused 88; the separate `check --help` usage refusal is
retained and excluded from those totals. Ordinary generic identity and CP
pass selected Raw but meet finite-profile limits. The first supposed positive
unused-generic case has a private entry and actually refuses host visibility.
Finite transformed-T cases meet a profile limit earlier than their predicted
semantic check. Those wrong predictions remain intact.

The 16-case v2 follow-up preauthored exact requests and independent matrices.
Its missing `common/Qargo.toml` blocks ten emissions. All 38 real invocations
remain: six emissions and six separate source checks succeed; artifact-only
exact requests accept two and refuse four. Ten dependent exact checks remain
unperformed because no artifact was emitted. This failed experiment supplies
no positive exact-T/CP conclusion.

The new v3 packet copies every v2 file unchanged and adds the enclosing
schema-2, edition-2026 manifest and a separate plan/freeze. All 16 programs,
requests and independent matrices remain unchanged. Its 48 fresh invocations
emit all 16 artifacts, accept all 16 separate source-step checks, and accept
the ten positive artifact requests while refusing the six negative requests.
There is no retry or weaker-request fallback within either observation window.
The earlier static addendum had chosen artifact-only requests before execution
because unrefined Raw emissions have empty source tables; its original
stronger source-snapshot hypothesis is still retained.

Exact native artifact requests cover T, adjoint/powers, controlled T, T beside
one owned reference, CP[1,3], structural permutation and physical SWAP. Wrong
global/inverse/erased T, wrong reference axis, whole-scalar CP and false SWAP
requests refuse. The independent R8 matrix files were **not** submitted to a
dense-matrix API. CP's symmetric diagonal does not distinguish exchanged owner
roles, and one reference case is not an arbitrary-reference theorem.

Descriptive artifact inspection records zero extra physical wires, Unit
pack/unpack around scalar-phase T, ordered maps, structural split/join routing,
and the three actual CNOTs of physical SWAP. T^8 retains eight source blocks;
its exact identity equation supplies no optimization or certified cost claim.
Those inspections are not target gate/depth/workspace certificates.

## Identity, bounds and retained limits

The first observations record CLI SHA-256
`738c573e71bc74b71ab2b69bc2f32480b80e5b053f1c3f3fa2ef502335b68cdf`
and observed HEAD `5d6c5c46a182275c08f9d8b4fd555a940fdb156a`.
The v2/v3 copied CLI records SHA-256
`601ec6e800e70d6d085c69c0fe568add0e2faa6429c02dd78ec7b420a71c6578`
and observed HEAD `79f4abeabfe8e721f68a3d39135d3fd04caa5ea2`.
Both record explicit kernel SHA-256
`54c9d60b80f67217abd95c8fe6ec1c06aa262e142d5e6db30f46a20cb90faf07`.
The v2/v3 CLI copy record describes a prior-HEAD build with reviewed working
changes; an observed HEAD is not an attestation that it built that binary.
The native JSON checker_identity is unpinned despite the externally captured
explicit binary hashes. Every observed source/binary window and predecessor
packet was stable in its recorded scope; this retention check does not inspect
today's compiler or execute an old binary.

All authored programs use at most two physical qubits. The first finite checks
may also check the existing unchanged bundled QFT3, explicitly allowed before
execution. Selected-only v2/v3 did not need it. Retention generates or checks no
quantum case. Successful source checks report native validity and source steps,
with source_meaning_verified=false and source_preservation_verified=false.
Successful exact checks concern independently requested emitted artifact maps,
with request_checked=true and source preservation still false.

No source-preservation, PR, quantitative RS or EXACT discharge, new guarantee,
hardware certification, full CI, release readiness or Issue completion is
claimed. The two admitted QLV1 ownership/classical-scope guarantees and broader
pending QS/PR/RS/EXACT obligations remain unchanged.

## Static retention reader

Run `python3 -B scripts/test_stdlib_boundary_first.py` from the repository root.
It never executes recorded commands. It validates the fixed manifest and
compressed/container/member hashes, every historical freeze, unchanged v2/v3
predecessors, real raw-stream bindings and bounded observation counts. It reads
at most 8 MiB of compressed data, 26 MiB of original content and 1,300 members,
with a bounded tar-container allowance before parsing. It extracts no files,
imports no retained runner, and rejects nonregular members and unsafe paths.
The repository's 150 MiB / 18,000-file fixture ceilings remain unchanged.

Archives use USTAR regular members sorted by path components, inert mode 0644, zero timestamps,
UID/GID and empty owner names, then gzip level 9 with an empty filename and zero
mtime. Original observed modes remain in the manifest. All six original
directories and their previous freeze inventories were verified before and
after retention. This is a new packet retention record, not a historical Git
archive baseline; no past commit or historical-source attestation is invented.
Fresh regressions must construct new commands and keep new results separately.
